Application Data.NAME: Harmony Arts Academy
Application Data.CONTACT FOR INSPECTION: Sarah Johnson, Director of Safety and Compliance
Application Data.DESCRIPTION OF OPERATIONS: Harmony Arts Academy offers a diverse range of dance, drama, and music classes for students of all ages, including ballet, jazz, contemporary dance, acting, and instrumental music. Our facility is equipped with state-of-the-art studios, practice rooms, and performance spaces designed to enhance the learning experience. We prioritize a safe and supportive environment, implementing strict supervision protocols, conducting thorough background checks on all instructors, and ensuring compliance with local safety regulations. We also provide regular training for our staff on safety procedures and risk management to minimize the potential for injuries during classes and performances. Our commitment to the well-being of our students is reflected in our proactive approach to safety and our dedication to fostering a positive artistic community.

Application Data.DESCRIPTION OF LOSSES: On 06/15/2021, a student slipped and fell during a ballet class due to an unmarked wet floor, resulting in a fractured wrist. The incident was reported immediately, and the student received medical treatment costing $5,000. The claim is currently in process, pending review by the insurance adjuster. Additionally, on 09/28/2022, a parent raised concerns about potential safety violations regarding supervision policies during a music recital. No claims were filed, but the issue remains unresolved, prompting additional scrutiny of safety protocols within the academy.
Application Data.OTHER PROTECTION: Security personnel on-site during classes and events; surveillance cameras installed throughout the facility; regular safety drills conducted.

Underwriting Guidelines:
– Entities with a poor safety record, including multiple prior claims related to bodily injury
or property damage, or known violations of local safety codes.
– Schools lacking formal supervision policies or failing to conduct background checks on
personnel working with minors.
Key Risk Considerations
Underwriters should evaluate the following exposures carefully, as
they represent the most frequent and severe claim drivers in this class:
• Bodily Injury Liability: Common claims arise from student slips, trips, and falls during
classes or rehearsals, as well as injuries related to the use of equipment such as ballet barres,
musical instruments, or stage props. For example, a dancer slipping on a wet floor or a student
tripping over unsecured cables during a music lesson.
• Abuse and Molestation Exposure: Particularly relevant for programs involving minors.
Insurers must assess the adequacy of background screening, supervision policies, and staff
